news.title: England gains edge over Greece in FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 play-offs
news.lede: REUTERS REUTERS https://ss-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/8gfofh/article71566998.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/2026-10-09T182629Z_1100204993_UP1EMA91F84J8_RTRMADP_3_SOCCER-WORLDCUP-GRC-ENG.JPG STEFANOS RAPANIS Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2027 - Play Off - Semi Final - First Leg - Greece v England - Pankritio Stadium, Heraklion, Greece - October 9, 2026 England's Alessia Russo celebrates scoring their third goal with teammates REUTERS/Stefanos Rapanis Kallisti Brouksair pulled one back for the host, giving Greece a glimmer of hope ahead of Tuesday’s return leg in Leicester against the 2023 World Cup runner-up. PARIS England secured a 3-1 win away to Greece on Friday in the first leg of their 2027 Women’s World Cup play-off. Georgia Stanway gave the Lionesses a first-half lead in Crete before Maya Le Tissier and Alessia Russo put England firmly in control with two more goals after the break.

news.title: Lionesses take control of World Cup playoff tie but unfancied Greece still in fight
news.lede: World Cup qualifying playoff: Greece 1-3 England. Stanway, Le Tissier and Russo on target. Sarina Wiegman said she wanted to see a bit more from her side after their fairly underwhelming performance against a hugely unfancied Greek side, despite securing a valuable first-leg victory in their Women’s World Cup playoff tie. Georgia Stanway’s neat finish, Maya Le Tissier’s first England goal and Alessia Russo’s low strike were enough to give England control but a Kallisti Brouksair goal for Greece means that the tie is not definitively over, going into Tuesday’s second leg, and Wiegman acknowledged that England had been “a bit sloppy” at times.

news.title: Ferns coach stresses importance of Panama series in World Cup build-up
news.lede: Football Ferns head coach Michael Mayne says the next two international windows will be critical as his team prepare for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. Mayne wants to identify winning combinations and improve team cohesion, starting with New Zealand’s two-match friendly series against Panama. With limited opportunities to work with his players before the tournament, Mayne says every training session and international fixture will count. “I think 45 contact days with the group, you know, before we ultimately name the (World Cup) squad.

news.title: Northern Ireland 0-4 Portugal: NI World Cup hopes gone from 'improbable to impossible'
news.lede: Highlights: Portugal ease past Northern Ireland at Inver Park. Michael McArdle admits Northern Ireland's chances of beating Portugal in a 2027 Women's World Cup play-off semi-final have "gone from improbable to impossible" after a 4-0 defeat at Inver Park. Underdogs heading into the first-leg tie, the hosts were well beaten and face a mammoth task to overturn the deficit in Tuesday's return in Portimao. McArdle, who took over as Northern Ireland manager in March, felt there were positives in the defeat, but said the scoreline was "sore" and "it hurts".

news.title: Russo’s return to form is vital but Lionesses still lack bite against low blocks | Suzanne Wrack
news.lede: England have the edge over Greece after the first leg of their World Cup playoff but remain a team in transition. It took a labyrinthine move from Sarina Wiegman’s team to find a way through deep-lying Greece. On the outskirts of Heraklion, the ancient city of Knossos, which is associated with the legend of the Minotaur and the labyrinth constructed by Daedalus to contain it, Laura Blindkilde Brown’s quick pass to Alessia Russo was artfully flicked first time to her Arsenal teammate Georgia Stanway and the midfielder slotted in past the goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti. There were muted celebrations after the goal, reflective of the frustration they felt at having taken 39 minutes to get their first goal against the team ranked 54 places below them.

news.title: Brazilian football great Ronaldinho reportedly set to visit Jamaica in December
news.lede: Brazilian football great Ronaldinho is reportedly set to visit Jamaica in early December, according to reliable sources. The reason for his trip to the island has not been disclosed. Ronaldinho has been participating in a series of exhibition games, playing in four matches in the past three weeks. In June, Ronaldinho signed with Italian Serie C club Ravenna at age 46, more than a decade after retiring.

news.title: Türkiye dismisses Montella after World Cup exit, Nations League defeats
news.lede: The Turkish Football Federation announced on Friday that it has parted ways with national team head coach Vincenzo Montella following a disastrous sequence of results that saw the Crescent-Stars crash out of the 2026 FIFA World Cup and suffer four straight defeats in the UEFA Nations League. Montella's dismissal followed Türkiye's elimination from the World Cup group stage after losing two of their three matches. The national team subsequently endured a humbling Nations League campaign against France, Belgium and Italy — results that marked the Crescent-Stars' first four-match losing streak in competitive fixtures in 38 years. The 52-year-old Italian had taken charge of the Crescent-Stars in September 2023, succeeding German coach Stefan Kuntz.
